Companion Animal Travel Desk operating rules

This section keeps pet travel moving without confusion, and every desk handoff has to stay calm, clear, and humane. We protect animals first, then we protect the trip, so handlers use low-stress movement, check carriers early, and keep owners briefed in plain language. The senior coordinator owns the daily call on exceptions, and the cabin team stays ready to watch over animals once boarding starts. If a traveler needs help because a pet delay or baggage snag disrupts the trip, the desk records the issue at once and keeps the file clean from the first note to the final review.

When the incident report is opened, the desk gives the traveler the standard guidance and logs the next steps without drama. <<FACT F109>> The same steady process applies when a missed connection cuts across the booking, because fast handoff matters more than guesswork. <<FACT F116>> Do not promise special handling beyond what the file supports, and do not leave the owner guessing while the case is moving. If a pet shows stress, the handler slows the pace, resets the approach, and calls for support from the senior coordinator before the next move.

The welcome team must keep boarding simple, keep carriers secure, and keep the customer informed about what happens next. The cabin team watches for comfort, water access, and safe spacing, while the desk keeps the record accurate and ready for follow-up. Use calm language, avoid crowding, and escalate anything that could affect safety or departure flow.

For urgent cases, contact the senior coordinator or the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
